note: Devias's light, laid over lighting.json while a character stands in Devias (game/world/maps.h, app/modes/play_mode.cpp). The base sheet is Lorencia's moonlit night; Devias is a snowfield under a winter day. MU draws it on a light snowy-blue clear and fog colour, (0.75, 0.85, 1.0) (SceneManager.cpp:383), and paints its cold into TerrainLight -- mean (115, 149, 178), the bluest of the three maps -- so the ground carries its own blue and the sun here stays near white. The snow is the brightest albedo in the game, so the exposure sits lower than Noria's and the bloom threshold just over one: a snowfield that clips reads as white paper, not snow. The sun is low, as a winter sun is, for long blue shadows across the drifts. The shade leans cold and the light a touch warm, which is what keeps snow from reading grey. The haze is MU's snowy blue at a trace, short of Noria's 0.0022 that was too strong. Invention on MU's look; first cut 2026-09-29, before the snowstorm, which will come in as devias_rain.json's weather blend. The grass: Frosted, not green (the user, 2026-09-29: 'green will not work'). MU grows its white tuft only on TileGrass02, the smoother snow (grass_slots in devias.json). The sward's blades carried the whole way to the frost colours, so no green survives from the sheet: a frozen grey-green root and a white-blue tip that catches the sun. They are gains and not colours: the grade keeps the blade sheet's own value, 0.06 in linear light (sward.py paints green), so white takes about thirteen to reach snow's 0.8 -- at 1.0 the field came out black. No straw, no meadow flowers in snow, shorter and thinner than a lawn, and a little glossier at the tip for rime. With the firs standing (2026-09-29): MU's TerrainLight is cobalt and cyan in the woods and it lights the objects as well as the ground, so the frame went electric blue -- saturation 1.0 to 0.82, the shade's cold eased, and the grass's gains made neutral, since the baked light already brings the blue. The water holds still (water_flow 0), as Noria's does, at the user's asking: MuMain slides every water tile a sheet in twenty seconds, which on a small pool reads as a river in a hole. 'some snowy dust also but minimal': the haze 0.0014 to 0.0018 and whiter, (0.86, 0.91, 1.0), still short of Noria's 0.0022 that was too strong. 'devias procedual grass is to dark, it has to blend with snow': the root was a mid grey under a 0.62 occlusion floor, so every blade was a dark stroke on white. The root taken nearly to the tip (gains 11 to 14) and the floor to 0.92, so the blades are the snow's own white and read by their shading alone, as frosted grass half-buried in it. 'more variations with length, not so much visible, maybe without ice effect': the ice was the glossy tips (roughness 0.35) and fs_grass's back-lit leaf green, which on white read as teal crystal -- the tips matte at 0.9 and the back light off (grass_through 0, a knob now, a leaf's green by default). Length: the sward down to 0.2 m with a quarter of the cards growing rank (twice as tall) where Lorencia has one in twelve, so the field is mostly stubble with stalks through it; and thinner, density 0.55 to 0.4. 'grass still looks kind of active': frozen grass does not wave -- the wind 0.16 to 0.04, a stir and no more, the lean 0.10 to 0.06, the field thinner again at 0.32, and no patch-to-patch colour swing (grass_vary 0). 'dont look to natural, look like ice blades': the blade sheet cut to a narrow card is a spike, and white spikes are ice. So Devias draws MU's own painted tuft, World3's TileGrass02.OZT -- soft curved grass under a dusting of snow -- as MU2's Turf did (grass_painted 1), in MU's own paint (grass_colour 0), on a wider card (aspect 0.9) so a tuft reads as a tuft, 0.26 m. 'more lush, more length variations, more transparent': density 0.32 to 0.6; a lower sward at 0.22 m with 35% of the cards rank, twice as tall, so short and tall stand mixed; and the cutout 0.28 to 0.42, which keeps only the cores of MU's soft painted strokes, so the snow shows through a tuft instead of behind a plate. Then 'more lush and more variation with lengths' twice: density to its most, 1.0, and half the cards rank over a 0.2 m sward -- a card's own draw spreads 0.46 to 1.48 of that and rank doubles it, so ankle-high stubble and half-metre stalks stand mixed. Then the user: 'in lorencia and noria they looked great, we need same effects but with snow grass'. So the painted tuft is gone again and Devias grows Lorencia's own sward -- its height, density, lean, rank and wind, all at the base sheet's numbers -- with only the colour changed: the blades carried wholly to a snow white (gains 9 to 14 on the blade sheet's 0.06), the root a little deeper for depth, no back-lit green, no straw, no tropical tints and no meadow flowers. The length spread a touch wider at 1.3 (grass_length_spread, a knob now, 1 elsewhere). 'yes, good. but shorter' -- 0.28 m tried, then 'taller was better': Lorencia's 0.42 kept. 'can we mix short ones and tall ones?': each card's own length spread 1.9 about the mean -- stubble at an eighth of the sward beside cards near twice it -- and one card in five rank at 2.2 times, where Lorencia has one in twelve at 1.85. At 1.9, one in five and 2.2 the rank stalks, wide as well as tall, stood hip-high as crystals: eased to 1.7, one in seven, 2.0. 'too tall': the sward 0.36 m, spread 1.6, one card in eight rank at 1.6 -- the mix of short and tall kept, the tops brought down. 'too tall' again: 0.30 m, rank 1.5. Then 'perfect' and 'now too short again': between the two, 0.34 m, rank 1.55. 'snow dust effect' -- the user meant Lorencia's and Noria's overall screen haze, not puffs on the ground (tried and taken out): Lorencia's is 0.0055 in brown, and Devias's 0.0018 was about two per cent at MU's camera distance and invisible. 0.004 in a snowy white-blue, (0.88, 0.92, 1.0). 'increase sun power little bit on daytime' (2026-09-30): the sun 3.4 to 3.8.
